title: React: Handle render identifier in manifest snippet generation
body:
## What I did

Fixed a bug where stories using `render: Template` (an identifier referencing a function) instead of an inline arrow/function expression would throw an error in the manifest snippet generation:

```
Expected render to be an arrow function or function expression
  > 46 |     render: Template,
       |             ^^^^^^^^
```

This pattern is legitimate CSF3 — the `csf-2-to-3` codemod even creates it when converting `Template.bind({})`.

## How it works

When `render` is an identifier:
1. Try to resolve it to its local declaration via `resolveIdentifierInit()`
2. If resolved to a function → use it (snippet includes the inlined JSX with args)
3. If unresolvable (e.g. imported) → gracefully fall back to no-function JSX synthesis

Also renamed `resolveBindIdentifierInit` → `resolveIdentifierInit` since it's now reused for both `Template.bind({})` and `render: Template` patterns.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:

- [ ] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [ ] integration tests
- [ ] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing

4 new unit tests covering all combinations:
- Story-level `render: Template` with local function → resolves and inlines JSX ✅
- Story-level `render: Template` with unresolvable identifier → graceful fallback ✅
- Meta-level `render: Template` with local function → resolves and inlines JSX ✅
- Meta-level `render: Template` with unresolvable identifier → graceful fallback ✅

All 40/40 tests passing.

comments.body: Good catch\! Implemented the tri-state approach in 40bab5e — getRenderPath now returns { kind: 'missing' | 'resolved' | 'unresolved' } so an unresolvable story-level render doesn't fall back to meta's render. Added a dedicated test for this scenario too.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment identifies a bug where an unresolved render identifier is indistinguishable from a missing render property, causing incorrect fallback to meta.render. It proposes a concrete fix using a tri-state resolution type to distinguish the two cases.
